defs: adj	(figurative) Calm, undisturbed, peaceful, serene.
n	(poetic) A kingfisher whose nesting by the sea was said, in classical mythology, to cause the Gods to restrain the wind and waves.
n	A tropical kingfisher of the genus Halcyon, such as the sacred kingfisher (Halcyon sancta) of Australia.
adj	Pertaining to the halcyon or kingfisher.
n	The dead body of such a bird, said in Tudor times to act as a weather vane when hung from a beam.
adj	Satisfied, pleased, contented.
n	Satisfaction, contentment; pleasure.
n	That which contents or satisfies; that which if attained would make one happy.
n	Subject matter; semantic information (or a portion or body thereof); that which is contained in writing, speech, video, etc.
n	(by extension, uncountable) One or more creative works.
n	(Internet, colloquial) The potential of creative work for a content creator.
n	The amount of material contained.
n	(uncountable) That which is contained.
n	(UK, House of Lords) An expression of assent to a bill or motion; an affirmative vote.
n	(UK, House of Lords, by metonymy) A member who votes in assent.
v	(transitive) To give contentment or satisfaction to; to satisfy; to make happy.

n	(mathematics) The n-dimensional space contained by an n-dimensional polytope (called volume in the case of a polyhedron and area in the case of a polygon); length, area or volume, generalized to an arbitrary number of dimensions.

n	(algebra, ring theory, of a polynomial with coefficients in a GCD domain) The greatest common divisor of the coefficients; (of a polynomial with coefficients in an integral domain) the common factor of the coefficients which, when removed, leaves the adjusted coefficients with no common factor that is noninvertible.
n	(obsolete) Acquiescence without examination.
v	(transitive, obsolete) To satisfy the expectations of; to pay; to requite.
adj	(obsolete) Contained.
n	(obsolete) Capacity for containing.
adj	Emitting much light; visually dazzling; luminous, lucent, radiant.
adj	Of light: brilliant, intense.
adj	Of an object, surface, etc.: reflecting much light; having a high lustre; gleaming, shiny.
adj	Of a place: not dark; well-lit.
adj	Of climate or weather: not cloudy or gloomy; fair; also, of a period of time, the sky, etc.: characterized by much sunshine and good weather.
adj	(transferred senses, figuratively)
adj	Clearly apparent; conspicuous.
adj	Of a colour: not muted or pale; bold, brilliant, vivid.
adj	Of an object, surface, etc.: having vivid colour(s); colourful.
adj	Of a musical instrument, sound, or a voice: clearly audible; clear, resounding, and often high-pitched.
adj	Of a room or other place: having acoustic qualities that tend to cause much echoing or reverberation of sound, particularly at high frequencies.
adj	Of a scent or taste: having an agreeable balance of sweet and sour, often with associations of coolness, freshness, and sometimes aromaticity.
adj	Of a scent or taste: not bland or mild; bold, sharp, strong.
adj	Of a substance: clear, transparent; also, pure, unadulterated; (specifically) of wine: free of suspended particles; not cloudy; fine.
adj	Glorious; illustrious.
adj	In good spirits; happy, optimistic.
adj	Of the face or eyes, or a smile: showing happiness or hopefulness; cheerful, lively.
adj	Of a person: lively, vivacious.
adj	Of a period of history or time: happy, prosperous, successful.
adj	Of an opportunity or outlook: having a reasonable chance of success; favourable, good.
adj	Of conversation, writing, etc.: imaginative or sparkling with wit; clever, witty.
adj	Having a clear, quick intellect; intelligent.
adj	(music) Of a rhythm or tempo: lively, upbeat.
adj	(music) Of a note: slightly sharp.
adj	(metallurgy) Of a metal object or surface: lacking any protective coating or surface treatment for the prevention of corrosion.
n	(chiefly in the plural) Something (especially a product intended for sale) that has vivid colours or a lustrous appearance.
n	A person with a naturalistic worldview with no mystical or supernatural elements.
n	(painting) An artist's brush used in acrylic and oil painting with a long ferrule and a flat, somewhat tapering bristle head.
adv	(often literary) In a bright manner; brightly, glowingly, luminously, lustrously.
adv	(figuratively) Referring to colour: with bold or vivid colours; brightly, boldly, vividly.
v	(transitive) Often followed by up: to cast light on (someone or something); to brighten, to illuminate.

v	(transitive, figuratively) Often followed by up: to cause (someone or something) to be bright (in various senses); to brighten; specifically, to make (someone or something) energetic, or happy and optimistic.
v	(intransitive, also figuratively) Often followed by up: to become bright (in various senses); to brighten.
adj	(archaic) Of the eyes: able to see clearly; of eyesight: keen, sharp.
adj	(archaic) Manifest to the mind as light is to the eyes; clear, evident, plain.
n	(archaic or literary) Brightness, glow.
n	(archaic or literary) (figuratively) Glory, splendour.
adv	(figuratively) (archaic) Referring to sight, sound, understanding, etc.: clearly, distinctly; brightly.
n	A surname.
n	A census-designated place in Dearborn County, Indiana, United States.
n	An unincorporated community in Roane County, West Virginia, United States.
n	An unincorporated community in Green Grove, Clark County, Wisconsin, United States.
n	A civil parish in York County, New Brunswick, Canada.
n	A town in Alpine Shire, north-east Victoria, Australia.
n	A civil parish and townland in County Down, Northern Ireland.
adj	Appropriate, apt, fitting.
adj	Causing happiness or pleasure.
adj	Auspicious, fortunate, lucky.
adj	Characterized by felicity.
adj	(linguistics) Of a sentence or utterance: semantically and pragmatically coherent; fitting in the context.
adj	Mirthful, cheerful, smiling, light-hearted.
adj	Of a place, landscape or view: having a pleasant appearance, looking bright or cheerful.
